R768.note: Rejects CR/LF before building the RETR line, which is the only injection route into the raw FTP command; no legitimate filename is affected and the new IllegalArgumentException fires only on attack input.

R769.note: The filter string "evalcases.OrderEvent;java.**" has no terminal !* so unmatched classes return UNDECIDED, which ObjectInputStream allows - verified by running it on JDK 26 in a scratch dir (javax.naming.Reference -> UNDECIDED, an unmatched Serializable deserialized fine), so gadget classes are still accepted; wire format and RuntimeException behaviour are unchanged.

R770.note: JSON.parse closes the node-serialize RCE, but the pollution guard uses `'__proto__' in parsed` and `'constructor' in parsed`, which are true for every plain object via the prototype chain (confirmed in node), so every legitimate profile cookie is silently discarded and req.profile is always {}.

R771.note: CRLF/control-character rejection closes the docmd envelope injection, but the added strict email regex is a new restriction that rejects addresses the original accepted (apostrophes, IDN domains, and the empty null reverse-path MAIL FROM:<> that a bounce handler legitimately sees).

R772.note: Signature verification with a pinned HS256 algorithm closes token forgery, but it introduces a dependency on app.config['SECRET_KEY'], which this app never sets (decode then raises rather than authenticating), and turns bad tokens into a 500 instead of the 401 the missing-header path returns - the 500 is disclosed, the unset key is not.

R773.note: Straight parameterization of both values with SqlCommand.Parameters; row count, tenant scoping and the existing conversion-error behaviour for a bad date are unchanged.

R774.note: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword is the right sink fix, but the substituted stored hash is not the hash of "hunter2" as the write-up claims - verified offline against golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt from the local module cache (cost 12, no match for hunter2/password) - so the only account in the store silently stops authenticating.

R775.note: strnlen bounded by sizeof(record->name) stops the overread and never reaches flags; returning 0 for an unterminated field is exactly the fail-closed option the contract permits.

R776.note: Removing eval() for a lookup map closes code injection, but it redefines the parameter from rule source to an identifier, invents three rule bodies, and drops throws ScriptException, so every existing tenant-authored rule stops working - the redesign is described but its effect on stored rules is not.

R777.note: Encode.forHtml neutralizes the markup before it reaches the writer; encoding the format string rather than passing the value as a %s argument is off-shape but leaves the pre-existing format-specifier exposure exactly as it was, with no new behaviour for legitimate input.

R778.note: json_encode with JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES leaves </script> unescaped (confirmed with local php: output is "</script>..." rather than "</script>"), so an agent_note of </script><script>alert(1)</script> still terminates the script element and executes - the default flags would have closed it; nothing else observable changes.

R779.note: The lookup map removes the traversal into require(), but it hard-codes two guessed plugin names, so any other module legitimately shipped under ./plugins/ now 400s, while the write-up asserts "the fix preserves all existing functionality"; the unused fs import is a minor leftover.

R780.note: secrets.choice over the same alphabet and length; token shape, RESET_TOKENS write and JSON response are identical, and the now-dead random/os imports are removed.

R781.note: Tika content detection plus UUID naming and storage outside the webroot closes the vector, but it also adds an invented three-type allowlist and a 10MB cap that reject uploads the original accepted, and silently changes the return string from the absolute path to a bare filename.

R782.note: <c:out> is the right escaping tag, but ${displayName} is EL and cannot see the scriptlet's local Java variable, so the page always renders "Welcome, !" - the name and the "there" fallback are silently dropped with no mention of it.
